description: A single-panel line plot (no sub-panels) showing dynamic-recrystallization (DRX) average grain size as a function of deformation temperature for the low-density high-strength Fe–Mn–Al–C steel. The x-axis is labelled "Temperature/°C" with tick marks at 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150; the y-axis is labelled "Grain size/µm" with ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60 and 80. Four curves are plotted, distinguished in the legend by strain rate: 0.01 s⁻¹ (black open squares), 0.1 s⁻¹ (red open circles), 1 s⁻¹ (blue open triangles) and 10 s⁻¹ (magenta open stars). Every curve rises monotonically with temperature, and at every temperature the grain size ranks 0.01 s⁻¹ > 0.1 s⁻¹ > 1 s⁻¹ > 10 s⁻¹. At 900 °C all four points lie low, near the bottom of the axis between the 0 and 20 µm gridlines (lowest for 10 s⁻¹); by 1150 °C the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve has climbed to just under the 80 µm gridline, well above 70 µm, whereas 10 s⁻¹ remains only slightly above the 20 µm gridline. The plot therefore demonstrates that coarse DRX grains form at low strain rate combined with high temperature.

subfigures.description: Single line plot of DRX average grain size (µm, y-axis, 0–80) versus temperature (°C, x-axis, 900–1150) with four strain-rate curves: 0.01 s⁻¹ (black squares), 0.1 s⁻¹ (red circles), 1 s⁻¹ (blue triangles), 10 s⁻¹ (magenta stars). All curves increase with temperature; the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve reaches the highest value (just below 80 µm) at 1150 °C.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line plot with x-axis labelled 'Temperature/°C' (ticks 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100, 1150) and y-axis labelled 'Grain size/µm' (ticks 0, 20, 40, 60, 80).
The legend contains four entries printed as '0.01 s⁻¹' (black open squares), '0.1 s⁻¹' (red open circles), '1 s⁻¹' (blue open triangles) and '10 s⁻¹' (magenta open stars).
All four curves increase monotonically with increasing temperature between 900 °C and 1150 °C.
At every measured temperature the grain size is largest for 0.01 s⁻¹ and smallest for 10 s⁻¹, i.e. the ranking is 0.01 s⁻¹ > 0.1 s⁻¹ > 1 s⁻¹ > 10 s⁻¹.
At 900 °C all four data points sit in the lower part of the plot between the 0 and 20 µm gridlines, with the 10 s⁻¹ point lowest and the 0.01 s⁻¹ point highest.
At 1150 °C the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve lies just below the 80 µm gridline and the 10 s⁻¹ curve only slightly above the 20 µm gridline; the two intermediate curves fall between them.
No numeric data labels are printed at the individual data points; values can only be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows the dynamic recrystallization average grain size of the steel under different T and ε̇.
The citing text states that the DRX grain size of the steel after hot deformation increases with the decrease of ε̇ or the increase of T.
The citing text states that when T is 1150 °C and ε̇ is 0.01 s⁻¹ the grain size exceeds 70 µm and the structure is coarse grain, indicating rapid growth of the recrystallized grains.
The citing text states that at low T (900–950 °C) and high ε̇ (1–10 s⁻¹) the DRX grains are small, DRX is not sufficient, large original grains remain and microstructure homogeneity is poor.
The citing text states that grain size was measured from the core of the compressed sample (the large deformation zone) after hot compression to 60%.
